articles.text: MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Duìbuqǐ, nǐ shi cóng Zhōngguó láide liúxuéshēng ba?
AMERICAN STUDENT: Excuse me, you must be a student from China, aren't you?
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Shì a! Nǐde Zhōngwén zènme hǎo, qùguo Zhōngguó ba?
CHINESE STUDENT: Yes! Your Chinese is so good! Have you been to China?
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Hái méiyou, yǐhòu yǒu jīhui wǒ yídìng yào qù kànkan.
AMERICAN STUDENT: Not yet, but if I get the chance to I'm sure I'll go visit.
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Nà nǐde Zhōngwén jiù shi zài Huáshèngdùn xuéde?
CHINESE STUDENT: Then you learned all your Chinese here in Washington?
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Èng. Jǐnián yǐqián wǒ zài Jiāzhōu Dàxué xuéguo yìnián, lái Huáshèngdùn yǐhòu yòu yìzhí zài xué. Kěshi Zhōngwénde shuǐpíng háishi bú gòu gāo.

AMERICAN STUDENT: Mm. A few years ago I had a year of Chinese at the University of California, and since I came to Washington, I've been studying it all along. But my level in Chinese still isn't high enough.
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Nǐ méiyou qùguo Zhōngguó, Zhōngwén zènme hǎo le, wǒ lái Měiguó yǐjīng yìnián, Yīngwén shuǐpíng háishi tígāode hěn màn.
CHINESE STUDENT: Your Chinese is this good and you've never been to China, but I've been in the States a year already and my English level is still improving very slowly.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Zài Zhōngguóde shíhour nǐ xuéguo Yīngwén ba?
AMERICAN STUDENT: You studied English when you were in China, I suppose?
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Xuéguo, xuéguo sānnián bàn ne!
CHINESE STUDENT: Sure, I studied it for three and a half years!
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Shi Yīngguó Yīngwén?
AMERICAN STUDENT: British English?
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Shì, érqiě jiàoshī yě dōu shi Zhōngguó rén, suǒyǐ chū guó yǐhòu zuì dàde wèntí shi tīngbudǒng, shuōbuchūlái. Kàn shū bǐ shuō huà róngyiduō le.

CHINESE STUDENT: Yes, and my teachers were all Chinese, so after I left China my biggest problem was that I couldn't understand people talking and I couldn't speak. Reading is a lot easier than speaking.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Zài Zhōngguóde shíhou, nǐ zài něige dàxué niàn shū?
AMERICAN STUDENT: In China, what university were you studying at?
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Zài Běidà.
CHINESE STUDENT: At B.U.
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Běidàde Yīngwén bān bànde bú cuò, búguò, wǒmen xué kējìde xuésheng zhòngdiǎn shi kàn shū, fānyì, bú shi huìhuà.
CHINESE STUDENT: B.U. is pretty good for English, but for us students in science and technology the emphasis is on reading and translating, not on conversation.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Kējì? Shì bu shì kēxué jìshu?
AMERICAN STUDENT: "Kējì"? Is that science and technology?
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Shì. Wǒmen chángcháng yòng hěn duō jiǎnchēng, duìbuqǐ ya!
CHINESE STUDENT: Right. We use a lot of abbreviations, pardon me!
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Nà méiyou shénme. Búguò wǒ hái yǒu yìdiǎnr bù dǒng.
AMERICAN STUDENT: No problem. But there's still something I don't understand.
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Shénme dìfangr?
CHINESE STUDENT: What?
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Nǐmen cháng shuō kēxué fēn liǎngbùfen, yíbùfen shi shèhuì kēxué, yíbùfen shi zìrán kēxué. Nàme kēxué jìshu shuōde jiù shi zìrán kēxué ma?
AMERICAN STUDENT: You often say that science has two divisions. One is social science and the other is natural science. So does science and technology refer only to the natural sciences?
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Zhè bú shi nàme yán'géde, tèbié shi xiàndài shèhuì, zìrán kēxué hé shèhuì kēxué jiù fēnde bú nàme qīngchu le.
CHINESE STUDENT: This distinction isn't so strict. Especially in modern society, the natural sciences and the social sciences aren't so clearly separated.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Zhè wǒ tóngyì. Zài fēn lèide wèntíshang, wǒmen yǒu hěn duō shuōfǎ hé nǐmen bú tài yíyàng.
AMERICAN STUDENT: I agree with that. On questions of categorization, we have a lot of ideas that are different from yours.
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Ōu, chē lái le, wǒ yào shàng chē le. Yǐhòu yǒu jīhui zài tán.
CHINESE STUDENT: Oh, here comes the train. I have to get on it. In the future we'll talk some more if we get the chance.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Hǎode, xiàcì wǒmen yòng Yīngwén tán.
AMERICAN STUDENT: All right. Next time we'll talk in English.
ZHŌNGGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Hǎo, xièxie ni, zàijiàn.
CHINESE STUDENT: Okay, thank you. Good-bye.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Zàijiàn.
AMERICAN STUDENT: Good-bye.
